written.myAnswer: The car experiences greater centripetal force on the curve with the smaller radius. Since F = mv²/r and the speed and mass are the same for both curves, the force is inversely proportional to the radius.
An accelerated body is not in equilibrium because it has a resultant force acting on it. In equilibrium, the resultant force is zero, so the body has no acceleration.
The taller box is more likely to tumble. Its centre of gravity is higher, so it is less stable and is more easily tipped when the truck stops suddenly.

An object is stable when its centre of gravity is low and its base of support is wide. It topples when the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base of support. For example, a racing car is made more stable by keeping its centre of mass low and spreading its wheels to give it a wider base; this makes it less likely to topple.
When the branch is shaken suddenly, the mango tends to remain at rest because of inertia. The relative motion can break the stalk, allowing the mango to fall.

Stability can be improved by lowering an object's centre of gravity and increasing its base area. Racing cars use a low centre of gravity and a wide base. A balancing toy is designed so that, when tilted, it returns to its stable position by lowering its centre of gravity.
The two principles are to keep the centre of mass as low as possible and to make the base of support as wide as possible.

In circular motion, velocity is along the tangent to the path. For uniform-speed motion, the force must not change the magnitude of velocity, so it can have no component along the velocity. Therefore, the centripetal force is perpendicular to the velocity.
